claim: AI models have been used to study the compositional regularities of proteins in nature.
source: Artificial intelligence (AI) models have been used to study the compositional regularities of proteins in nature, enabling it to assist in protein design to improve the efficiency of protein engineering and reduce manufacturing cost.
evidence: This is a general statement about AI applications in protein science, supported by the broader scientific literature and context of the study.

claim: In industrial settings, proteins are often required to work in extreme environments where they are relatively scarce or even non-existent in nature.
source: However, in industrial settings, proteins are often required to work in extreme environments where they are relatively scarce or even non-existent in nature.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about industrial protein requirements and the scarcity of naturally occurring extremophilic proteins.

claim: It is uncertain whether AI models possess the capability of evolving proteins to adapt to extreme conditions where such proteins are almost absent in training datasets.
source: Since such proteins are almost absent in the training datasets, it is uncertain whether AI model possesses the capability of evolving the protein to adapt extreme conditions.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the limitation of training data for AI models.

claim: Antibodies are crucial components of affinity chromatography.
source: Antibodies are crucial components of affinity chromatography, and they are hoped to remain active at the extreme environments where most proteins cannot tolerate.
evidence: This is established knowledge in biochemistry and biotechnology.

claim: The Pro-PRIME model was applied to improve the alkali resistance of a VHH antibody capable of binding to growth hormone.
source: In this study, we applied an advanced large language model (LLM), the Pro-PRIME model, to improve the alkali resistance of a representative antibody, a VHH antibody capable of binding to growth hormone.
evidence: This is directly stated as the main objective and method of the study.

claim: Through two rounds of design, the selected mutant has enhanced functionality, including higher thermal stability, extreme pH resistance, and stronger affinity.
source: Through two rounds of design, we ensured that the selected mutant has enhanced functionality, including higher thermal stability, extreme pH resistance, and stronger affinity, thereby validating the generalized capability of the LLM in meeting specific demands.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: This is the first LLM-designed protein product successfully applied in mass production.
source: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first LLM-designed protein product, which is successfully applied in mass production.
evidence: This is a claim made by the authors based on their knowledge of the field.

claim: Protein engineering focuses on the design of proteins to introduce novel functionalities or enhance existing attributes.
source: Protein engineering, situated at the nexus of molecular biology, bioinformatics, and biotechnology, focuses on the design of proteins to introduce novel functionalities or enhance existing attributes (Lovelock et al., 2022; Lutz and Iamurri, 2018; Tokuriki and Tawfik, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: Protein engineering has experienced a significant shift toward advanced computational methodologies, particularly deep learning.
source: With the exponential growth of biological data and computational power, protein engineering has experienced a significant shift toward advanced computational methodologies, particularly deep learning, to expedite the design process and unravel complex protein–function relationships (Jang et al., 2022; Li et al., 2023; Narayanan et al., 2021; Qiu and Wei, 2023; Tan et al., 2023; Zhou et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to recent literature.

claim: A significant challenge in industrial protein engineering is designing proteins with inherent resistance to extreme conditions, such as high temperature and extreme pH environments.
source: However, a significant challenge in industrial protein engineering is designing proteins with inherent resistance to extreme conditions, such as high temperature and extreme pH environments (acidic or alkaline) (Jaenicke, 1991; Pinney et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: Proteins used in industrial processes often encounter harsh physical and chemical conditions, necessitating exceptional resilience to maintain functionality.
source: Unlike proteins in natural ecosystems, those used in industrial processes often encounter harsh physical and chemical conditions, necessitating exceptional resilience to maintain functionality (Rao et al., 2021; Xia et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: Previous efforts to enhance protein resistance have often relied on rational design and mutant library screening, which are typically labor-intensive, inefficient, and yield limited improvements.
source: Previous efforts to enhance protein resistance have often relied on rational design and mutant library screening. These methods are typically labor-intensive, inefficient, and yield limited improvements (Gülich et al., 2002; Linhult et al., 2004; Minakuchi et al., 2013; Palmer et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: The industrial demand for proteins resilient to harsh environments poses a notable absence within the training datasets of AI models.
source: Consequently, the industrial demand for proteins resilient to harsh environments poses a notable absence within the training datasets of artificial intelligence (AI) models.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the nature of AI training data.

claim: Recent advances in large-scale protein language models have enabled zero-shot predictions of protein mutants based on self-supervised learning from natural protein sequences.
source: Recent advances in large-scale protein language models (LLMs) have enabled zero-shot predictions of protein mutants based on self-supervised learning from natural protein sequences (Hie et al., 2021; Madani et al., 2023; Rao et al., 2021; Rives et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: AI-guided protein design has been applied to predict mutants with greater thermostability and higher activity.

evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: It is unexplored whether AI models based on natural protein information can find mutants that adapt to unnatural extreme environments, such as alkaline solutions with pH higher than 13.
